definitions: An orthogonal projection on Euclidean R^3 is a real 3x3 matrix P with P^T=P and P^2=P.
A symmetric matrix D is positive semidefinite when x^T D x>=0 for every x in R^3.
Products and powers are ordinary matrix multiplication; the six displayed products average all permutations of the three labeled factors.
hypotheses: E,F,G are orthogonal projections on R^3.
There are no rank, distinctness, commutativity, mutual-orthogonality or sum-to-identity restrictions.
proposal.quantifiers: For every E,F,G in M_3(R) satisfying the projection equations, the conclusion holds for every x in R^3. Include ranks 0 through 3, zero and identity projections, and repeated projections.
